mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05) in the identified regime.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: In a robust labor recovery regime, the correlation between PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline is weak (Pearson < 0.3) or the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) relative to GDP (implied by INDPRO) indicates excess demand in the economy, which tends to push equity valuations higher over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate exceeds 2% while INDPRO remains flat or increases
failure_condition: The 5-day SPX forward return is not significantly different from its pre-expansion average (p > 0.05) when GDPC1/INDPRO dynamics match the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) over two consecutive months suggests weakening supply-side conditions, which often precedes a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as market anticipates policy easing.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO contracts for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 days (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO contraction is confirmed.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 0.3% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver negative 20-day forward returns as markets anticipate a pre-emptive rate hike by the Federal Reserve.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL inflation rate > 0.3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Inflation exceeds 0.3% for 3 months but SPX 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (HOUST) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) creates a labor market imbalance that typically boosts equity valuations over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE decreases
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not significantly higher than the 30-day average during similar labor market imbalances (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (implied by PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates demand-driven growth, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while INDPRO remains flat or declines
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when the trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive feedback loop where rising consumer sentiment (implied by a composite of HOUST and PAYEMS) consistently predicts higher S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days, regardless of macro regime.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not positively correlated with the sentiment composite (Pearson < 0.1) or the signal fails to predict returns in at least 70% of test windows (AUC < 0.7).
